text:
# Kitchen Packing List

## Keep Out Until Moving Day (Day-One Essentials)

These go in a clearly labeled box or bin that rides in your car, not the truck.

**Cooking and eating for the first night:** one pot, one pan, two plates, two bowls, two mugs, two sets of utensils, a spatula, a can opener, a sharp knife, and a cutting board. Add a roll of paper towels, dish soap, a sponge, and a dish towel. If you use a French press or pour-over, pack that too — you don't want to hunt for coffee on day two.

**Snacks and basics:** a few shelf-stable items for arrival night (pasta, jarred sauce, peanut butter, crackers, coffee, tea, sugar, salt, pepper, olive oil). Toss in a couple of trash bags and a roll of aluminum foil.

**Dog stuff that lives in the kitchen:** one bowl for food, one for water, a day's worth of food and treats, and any meds. These can share the same bin.

---

## Pack Early (Weeks 3–2 Out)

These are things you probably won't miss in the final weeks.

**Entertaining and seasonal items:** serving platters, punch bowls, cake stands, holiday dishes, fondue sets, specialty bakeware you use a few times a year.

**Small appliances you use rarely:** bread maker, waffle iron, ice cream maker, food processor if you mostly use a knife, slow cooker if you have an Instant Pot (or vice versa). This is also a great time to decide what to donate — if you haven't used it in a year, it probably doesn't need to cross the country.

**Cookbooks and decorative items:** anything on open shelves or above the cabinets.

**Extra pantry stock:** canned goods, spices you have duplicates of, baking supplies. Use what you can before the move and donate the rest rather than shipping heavy cans 2,400 miles.

---

## Pack Mid-Phase (Week 2)

**Bakeware:** muffin tins, cookie sheets, pie dishes, mixing bowls beyond the one you kept out.

**Most countertop appliances:** toaster, blender, stand mixer. Wrap cords and tape them to the appliance so they don't tangle.

**Glasses, wine glasses, and bar supplies:** wrap each glass individually in packing paper. Dish-pack boxes (the ones with cell dividers) are worth the money here.

**Most pots, pans, and lids:** keep your one daily-use pot and pan out, pack the rest. Nest pots with paper between them to prevent scratching.

**Utensil overflow:** whisks, tongs, ladles, rolling pins, and anything beyond the core set you kept out.

**Linens:** extra dish towels, cloth napkins, table runners. These make excellent padding between fragile items.

---

## Pack Last (Final 2–3 Days)

**The stuff you're still using daily:** your remaining everyday plates, the toaster you used this morning, the coffee maker, cleaning supplies under the sink, the trash can, and the last of the pantry.

**Cleaning supplies to keep until the very end:** an all-purpose spray, paper towels, and trash bags for the final walkthrough. These go in your car, not a box.

---

## Declutter Tips for the Kitchen

**The "move it 2,400 miles?" test:** hold up each item and ask whether you'd pay a few dollars to ship it across the country. Chipped mugs, duplicate spatulas, and that novelty apron fail this test quickly.

**Spices expire.** Check the bottoms — ground spices lose potency after about 2–3 years. Toss old ones and buy fresh in Oregon.

**Perishables can't come.** Plan meals around your freezer and fridge in the last two weeks. Give away what's left to neighbors or a local food pantry (they typically accept unopened, unexpired items).

**Donate, don't trash.** Goodwill, Habitat for Humanity ReStores, and local Buy Nothing groups will take working appliances, dishes, and cookware. Schedule a pickup or drop-off a week before the move so it's not a last-minute scramble.
